_comment: Alphadome digital drops. Prices are KES anchors; price_usd is a display anchor for diaspora buyers and is not charged through M-Pesa. Every published row needs a built asset in drops_assets/ (npm run drops:build) or the access page says so instead of pretending.

products.title: The AI Work Application Kit
products.summary: The 22-page pack that gets an AI-work application finished instead of abandoned. Built from a measured funnel where 159 people started an application and only 22 finished it.
outcomes: Know exactly what a Mercor-style application asks for before you open it
Have the four artefacts that shortlisters look for ready to paste
Write a rate and availability line that does not disqualify you
Recognise the three application shapes and which one your skills fit

modules.title: What the form will ask, in order
modules.detail: The seven questions that appear in almost every AI-work application, what each one is really screening for, and the two-sentence answer shape that survives a keyword filter and a human reader.

modules.title: The four artefacts
modules.detail: A one-page profile, two work samples with a one-line context note, and an availability block. Templates included, written for people whose work is under NDA or not public.

modules.title: Rate and availability
modules.detail: How to set a floor, when to quote hourly versus per task, and how to state time-zone overlap without promising hours you cannot keep.

modules.title: The assessment, taken once
modules.detail: How timed skills assessments are usually structured, a 45-minute practice set, and the failure pattern that loses otherwise-qualified candidates.

modules.title: After you submit
modules.detail: What the matching step looks like, how long silence usually lasts, when a follow-up helps, and the one message that gets a stalled application reopened.

practice: Fill the four artefacts for one real role today, before you look at a second application.
Time yourself writing the availability block; if it takes more than ten minutes, it is too complicated to keep.
Take the practice assessment on a phone, not a laptop, because that is how most people actually sit it.
Send one application and log the date, the role and the stage you reached. The log is what makes the next attempt faster.
products.delivery_note: One HTML pack, readable on a phone, with all five sections and the templates. Access for 12 months; re-download any time.

seo.title: What the AI-work application asks for, before you open it
seo.description: A measured look at why 86% of AI-work applications are abandoned, and the four artefacts that get one finished.

demand.note: The repo's own referral funnel: 159 applications started, 22 completed (13.8%), 3 hired, 0 paid. The blocker is discoverable late.

products.title: Alphadome Build Log 2026
products.summary: The engineering diary behind a multi-tenant WhatsApp and M-Pesa platform: what broke, what the measurement said, and the fix that shipped. Written from the commit history, not from a content calendar.
outcomes: See how a conversion engine was rebuilt after the data contradicted the copy
Copy the debugging pattern that turned a 40 MB request storm into one proxy setting
Understand the multi-tenant isolation choices and why they were forced
Use the same build-log structure to publish your own progress

modules.title: The blog was well written and did not convert
modules.detail: Two datasets — a referral funnel and 48 LinkedIn posts — that killed the content strategy, and the playbook module that replaced it.

modules.title: 299 pages, 38 of them fake
modules.detail: How verifier and smoke-test pages leaked into a public index, the audit that found them, and the predicate that keeps them out.

modules.title: The template that could not be pressed
modules.detail: 96 pages with no closing block and 21 with a button that went nowhere; the fixed-point rebuild that repaired them without a model call.

modules.title: Money paths are state machines
modules.detail: Why the M-Pesa callback is written as transitions, how duplicate callbacks are absorbed, and what idempotency cost in code.

modules.title: Publishing the log
modules.detail: The four-part post shape used here: measurement, contradiction, change, verification. With the checklist for what must never be claimed.

products.delivery_note: One HTML pack with five sections plus the source documents it was assembled from. Access for 12 months.

seo.title: A build log where the measurements changed the product
seo.description: Five engineering reversals from a WhatsApp and M-Pesa platform, written from the evidence rather than the roadmap.

demand.note: Buyers of implementation work read build logs before they book a call. This is the same asset sold as proof and as a product.

products.title: WhatsApp + M-Pesa Checkout Kit
products.summary: The implementation pack for taking a payment inside a WhatsApp conversation in Kenya: catalogue, STK prompt, callback state machine, receipt and reconciliation. Assembled from a system that runs it.
outcomes: Send a real M-Pesa prompt from your own shortcode and read the callback safely
Write an order row that survives a retried callback without double-delivering
Give every sale a merchant code that reconciles against your statement
Handle the failed prompt with a fallback instead of losing the customer

modules.title: The money lane, end to end
modules.detail: Daraja OAuth, the STK request body, the password timestamp, and the four environment variables that must agree. Includes the exact failure messages and what each one means.

modules.title: The callback as a state machine
modules.detail: Pending, prompted, paid, delivered, failed. Why the handler must acknowledge before it works, and how to absorb a duplicate callback.

modules.title: Order rows and reconciliations
modules.detail: The table shape, the account reference that fits Daraja's 12-character limit, and the merchant code that turns a statement line into a tenant.

modules.title: WhatsApp delivery
modules.detail: The message that goes out after payment, the 24-hour window constraint, and which templates must be pre-approved before launch.

modules.title: The failure path
modules.detail: Cancelled prompts, wrong PIN, insufficient funds, timeouts. The fallback sequence that recovers a sale instead of apologising for it.

products.delivery_note: One HTML pack: the five sections plus the source documents it was assembled from (payment links, scan-to-pay, the funnel play). Access for 12 months.

seo.title: Taking an M-Pesa payment inside WhatsApp, without a developer on call
seo.description: The STK prompt, the callback state machine and the reconciliation that make a WhatsApp sale collect money in Kenya.

demand.note: WhatsApp carries more than 20% of Kenya's online shopping orders (Mastercard/Flowcart, 2026), and 80% of Kenyan SMEs name simple payments as the top growth requirement.

products.title: Multi-Tenant WhatsApp Bot Starter
products.summary: The schema, the tenant middleware and the onboarding runbook for running one WhatsApp bot for many businesses without the data crossing. Taken from a system that onboards tenants for a living.
outcomes: Stand up bot_tenants, templates and training data without touching an existing schema
Route one webhook to the right tenant by phone number id
Onboard a client in an afternoon with a checklist that does not leak credentials
Add a second client without a redeploy or a second server

modules.title: The multi-tenant data model
modules.detail: Tenant, template, training and control tables; why every child row carries the tenant id; and the additive migration order that keeps a live bot running.

modules.title: Routing a webhook to a tenant
modules.detail: Phone number id to tenant resolution, the fallback when a number is unknown, and the logging that makes a misroute obvious in minutes.

modules.title: Secrets per tenant
modules.detail: Which credentials live in the database rather than the environment, how they are sealed, and what must never be returned by an API.

modules.title: Onboarding runbook
modules.detail: The exact credential request, the verification queries, and the three checks that decide whether a tenant is live or merely configured.

modules.title: Isolation you can prove
modules.detail: The test that attempts a cross-tenant read and must fail, plus the review checklist before a second client is allowed in.

products.delivery_note: One HTML pack with the five sections and the migration and runbook documents it was assembled from. Access for 12 months.

seo.title: One WhatsApp bot, many businesses, no crossover
seo.description: The schema and routing that let a single webhook serve many clients, and the test that proves isolation.

demand.note: Agencies reselling conversational commerce need the tenant layer before they can take a second client. This is the part that is usually rebuilt badly.

products.title: AI Agent Ops Track
products.summary: A self-paced, written track for the job that is actually being hired: agents that run in production, with tool use, evals, cost control and an on-call story. Six modules, six labs, no video you have to sit through.
outcomes: Build an agent loop with tool use, retries and a hard cost ceiling
Write evals that fail a bad agent before a customer does
Run a browser or API agent with credentials that cannot be exfiltrated
Write the operations page a hiring manager asks for: logs, alerts, rollback

modules.title: The loop, and where it breaks
modules.detail: Plan, act, observe, repeat: the four failure modes (looping, silent tool failure, context overflow, unbounded spend) and the guard each one needs. Lab: a task runner with a token budget.

modules.title: Tool use and MCP
modules.detail: Designing a tool surface an agent cannot misuse, validating arguments server-side, and when an MCP server is the right boundary. Lab: wrap an existing REST endpoint as a safe tool.

modules.title: Retrieval and memory
modules.detail: Chunking choices that change answer quality, the hybrid search baseline, and what to store versus recompute. Lab: a retrieval path with a citation requirement.

modules.title: Evals that gate a release
modules.detail: Golden sets, rubric grading, regression thresholds and cost-per-success. Lab: an eval suite wired to fail a pull request.

modules.title: Runtime and credentials
modules.detail: Tenant-scoped secrets, least privilege, the browser-agent pattern for systems with no API, and the audit trail that makes an incident survivable. Lab: a sealed credential store with a rotation test.

modules.title: Operating it
modules.detail: The dashboards, alert thresholds, retry and dead-letter policy, and the rollback that does not require a redeploy. Lab: an operations page for the agent you built.

practice: Pick one task you already do manually and write its tool surface before you write the prompt.
Put a hard token ceiling on the loop and log every time it is hit; the log is your first cost review.
Write five evals from real failures you have seen, not from imagined ones.
Draw the operations page on paper: what alerts, who is paged, what rollback means for this agent.
products.delivery_note: One HTML workbook: six modules, six lab briefs, the reading list and the review checklist. Written material, not recorded video. Access for 12 months, updated as the track changes.

seo.title: The agent operations work that is actually being hired for
seo.description: Six modules on agent loops, tool use, evals, runtime credentials and on-call, built from production failure modes.

demand.note: 2,401 open agentic roles across 194 companies in October 2026; agent engineering is 65% of the mix and agent ops/infra another 157 roles. Most-requested skills: Python (1,732), RAG (661), MCP (649), TypeScript (508), LangGraph (348), evals (301).
